title: The manager who gave the girls whiskey, and Margaret Warren
summary: The show's manager gave three girls whiskey in Coca-Cola; the older dancer Margaret Warren came in and beat him with a stick. Margaret watched over her again on the Harris show.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Well, did the man come to your house?
For the home talent, yes. They usually called - we didn't have a phone then - they got in touch. It seemed that everybody knew about me all over East Liberty and downtown.
Do you remember this man's name?
No, I don't remember his name and happy I forgot it, because he was not too nice with these kids.
He got you and the other girls in a room?
In a room and he was giving us whiskey and Coca-Cola, and Margaret came in. He was just about to do his act, you know, and she came into the room. I was so sick.
WILLIAMS

He put it in Cola-Cola and we thought we were drinking Coca-Cola. None of us knew the taste of whiskey. She came in and she took a stick and she was beating all over his head. Margaret Warren, she was beautiful. She was watching over us and we didn't even know it.
What became of the home talent show?
He was the one that got this home talent, the manager of the home talent.
Was this the beginning of it or the break-up of it?

No, the beginning of it was, we rehearsed and we did the home talent show in Pittsburgh. Then we ventured out to Washington, Pennsylvania, to a theatre there, to do the same show and he had all these young kids with him.
So was that as far as you got, just to Washington?
Yes. Margaret pulled out and took 3 of us home with her.
Did you work with her again?
Yes, with the Buzzin' Harris show, and I always had that same protection from her.
So this is another person that -?
Yes, Margaret Warren. She was such a beautiful person. She would walk over and you wouldn't even know it. She was so quiet and easy going, just a beautiful person.
What became of her, do you know?
WILLIAMS
She's still in Pittsburgh; I just saw her when I did the Mass there. She was dancing with the chorus, you see. She was teaching the girls. She was 18 herself but we were 14, 15 years old.
